clue.text: Classic queen of wild north-eastern people

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: N and E are the compass abbreviations for north and east
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legendary queen ruling over an untamed tribe from the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope, faithful wife of Odysseus, was queen of Ithaca in Greek myth, a figure from classical literature.

clue.text: Miss White's worried about everything, like tram-lines

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the jumbled name wraps the next word
something worried is agitated and disturbed, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: Pearl White was the star of the silent film serial The Perils of Pauline
everything is all

explanation.surface: An actress fretting about the whole world, nervous as tram tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearl White was a famous silent-screen heroine; her jumbled name PAREL splits as P...AREL around ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tram tracks run side by side at a constant distance and never meet, which is what lines running equidistant are.

clue.text: Enter it, if needing disguise, as Nile Queen

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so these letters must be rearranged to look different

parts.note: all nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to slip in disguised, playing an Egyptian queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was the royal wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten, so a queen of the ancient Egypt along the river.

clue.text: Gypsy Rose honoured by old doctor

parts.note: Gypsy Rose Lee was a famous American burlesque performer
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: A stripper receives an honour bestowed by a doctor of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honoured by old doctor' reads as one phrase, but 'old doctor' is the definition and 'by' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech was an archaic word for a physician, from the medical practice of bloodletting with leeches.

clue.text: Household gods — a set-up to support a writer

indicators.note: in a down entry, whatever supports another piece sits directly underneath it

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Domestic deities propped up by an arrangement to help an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To support' places the reversed phrase below PEN, as it sits underneath in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Penates were Roman deities guarding the family storeroom and home, worshipped alongside the Lares.

clue.text: Slated, having swung the camera

definitions.meaning: first meaning: harshly criticised, as by a reviewer
second meaning: moved a camera horizontally to follow action

explanation.surface: A film reviewed badly by critics after sweeping camera work.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both a critic savaging work and a cameraman rotating the lens across a scene.

clue.text: A cloudy halo, if the heavenly sign appears

parts.note: an is an archaic word for if, as in Shakespeare
the Lion, Leo, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A misty ring shows if a sign in the sky turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: AN for 'if' is an old usage solvers meet in crosswords; Leo the Lion is the zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthelion is a faint bright patch or ring seen on clouds or fog opposite the sun.

clue.text: Middleman's orange

definitions.note: possessive in form: the middle part of a man
definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as middle of a man, the belly button
second meaning: a seedless orange with a button-like mark at one end

explanation.surface: A broker's piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middleman' looks like an agent in trade, but split it: the man's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button sits at the centre of the body, and a variety of seedless orange shares the name.

clue.text: Issued new form for one in this

definitions.text: Issued new form for one in this

indicators.note: giving something a new form remakes it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something no longer used gets reissued in a new version.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes what to do with an item neglected and idle: bring it out again in a fresh form.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of no longer being employed, the condition an obsolete thing is in before reissue.

clue.text: Would they make the President feel at home in the far North?

definitions.text: Would they make the President feel at home in the far North?

parts.words: Would they make the President feel at home
parts.note: surface reading: a question about hospitality for a head of state on a visit
setter's reading: the dwellings anyone, president included, would live in among the Inuit of the Arctic

explanation.surface: A question about whether Arctic hosts could make a visiting president comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow houses are the traditional Inuit dwellings built in the Arctic, homes in the far North.

clue.text: Is this man a soldier looking for plunder?

definitions.note: a question: this word plus man makes a soldier
definitions.meaning: first meaning: add MAN to the answer and you have an infantryman
second meaning: to ransack or search through and steal

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man is a looting soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This man' reads as a person, but it means the answer followed by the word man, giving a soldier's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to go through it thoroughly stealing, as a looter does to a drawer or house.

clue.text: Evidence in camera? No, no!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the developed film from a camera, the photographic record
second meaning: each no is a refusal word

explanation.surface: A lawyer objecting to testimony heard in a closed court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In camera' is the legal phrase for a private hearing, but here it means inside a photographic camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed film strips hold the reversed photographic images, and refusals such as no are statements of denial.

clue.text: Movement of 4's associate to Jewish quarter

parts.note: 4 down is the household gods, always paired with the Lares; a single one is a Lar
a ghetto was the walled Jewish district of a city

explanation.surface: A household spirit relocating to a Jewish neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lares and Penates' is the set phrase for Roman household gods, hence the cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A larghetto is a musical piece or section played fairly slowly, and a section of a symphony is called a movement.

clue.text: Bell for Emily

parts.note: surface reading: a bell rung to summon a girl
setter's reading: the given name Emily Brontë used in her pen name with surname Bell

explanation.walkthrough: The Brontë sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell; Emily was the second of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë published Wuthering Heights under a male pseudonym whose first name is this word.

clue.text: The Avengers, right in among the 25s

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the first pair sits inside the last word

parts.note: 25 across is an observer, and eyes are what observe
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV spy show's heroes appearing right in front of the viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avengers suggests the 1960s TV series, but here it means the Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Erinyes, or Furies, were Greek goddesses of vengeance who hunted down wrongdoers.

clue.text: Cross the date-line going eastwards to visit it

definitions.text: Cross the date-line going eastwards to visit it

parts.note: surface reading: a travel instruction for a Pacific voyage
setter's reading: crossing the line eastwards sets the calendar back a day, so you reach the day before

explanation.surface: Travel advice about sailing east across the Pacific's international date-line.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading east over the International Date Line puts the calendar back one day, landing you in the previous day.

clue.text: Plan is to destroy this column

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; it describes this kind of column

indicators.note: destroying the words breaks them apart so their letters can be rebuilt differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scheme to demolish a pillar or newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: The backbone is called the spinal column, so the adjective names this column of vertebrae.

clue.text: Blue and green for seascape engravings?

definitions.text: Blue and green for seascape engravings?

parts.note: surface reading: the colours a painter would choose to depict the sea
setter's reading: prints made by an acid etching process, split as sea-water shades

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer and it reads as watery hues: aqua is blue-green, tints are shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatint is an etching technique producing tonal prints like watercolour, so these are such etched prints.

clue.text: Top of the bill? Rats

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the headline act on a theatre programme

definitions.note: a cryptic definition: the answer read as an instruction produces this word
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read the answer as an instruction, turn the bright celestial word round, and you get this word

explanation.surface: A headliner's name on the bill, followed by an exasperated curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' looks like an exclamation of annoyance, but it is what you get by following the answer as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The headline performer in a variety show is the leading act, billed most prominently on the poster.

clue.text: Part of its tail is somewhat flexible

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is taken, a run of letters lying across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: A description of an animal's tail being rather bendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' only sets the scene; the letters start in the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom means supple and lithe, able to bend easily, which is what something flexible is.

clue.text: Arty form of law

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a picture made from small coloured tiles

definitions.note: adjectival: describing the law given by Moses
definitions.meaning: second meaning: relating to Moses, as in the law he handed down

explanation.surface: An artistic type of legal procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiled pictures are a decorative art, and the capitalised adjective refers to Moses, giver of the biblical commandments.

clue.text: What copper wire will do, or lead

definitions.meaning: first meaning: transmit electricity or heat
second meaning: direct or guide, as an orchestra

explanation.surface: Choosing between copper and lead for electrical wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' sits beside 'copper' and wants to be the metal; it is the verb to guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Metals transmit electric current, and to direct an orchestra or tour is to guide it.

clue.text: Proved not guilty of falling at Becher's?

definitions.text: Proved not guilty of falling at Becher's?

parts.note: surface reading: a court verdict acquitting someone
setter's reading: a horse that jumped the fence safely got over it

explanation.surface: A jockey acquitted of blame for a fall in the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: Becher's Brook is a notorious fence on the Grand National steeplechase course at Aintree, near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant acquitted has their name restored, and a horse jumping a fence gets over it without touching it.

clue.text: 'ow to treat a borderline examinee everywhere

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in this spelling tells you to speak the same way, losing that sound

parts.note: a marginal candidate is let through by the examiner

explanation.surface: A Cockney asking how to handle a student who barely scraped through.
explanation.walkthrough: Without its aitch the phrase becomes the Latin word used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin used in references to mean a term occurs throughout a text, in many places.

clue.text: What one did in this dwelling

definitions.note: a past-tense verb: what one did
definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of abide, to live or stay
second meaning: a home or residence

explanation.surface: Wondering what someone got up to in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The old verb abide means to stay, with this past form, and the noun names a residence or home.

clue.text: Basket-maker found in bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a willow whose pliant rods are woven into wicker baskets
second meaning: a plant grown in a riverside willow plantation, which is called a bed

explanation.surface: A weaver of baskets discovered lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: This willow's flexible shoots are used for wickerwork, and willows are grown in planted plots called beds.

clue.text: Observer Bystander? Yes and no
Prohibition also includes tar

indicators.note: a word that includes another holds it inside itself

parts.note: also means too
a tar is a sailor, and AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A ban that covers tar as well as other substances.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar for a sailor is a crossword staple, as is AB for an able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a social or religious ban forbidding something, a prohibition by custom.

clue.text: Dervish dispensing with a bath-towel?

parts.note: surface reading: a whirling Sufi dancer
setter's reading: a whirling machine that gets washing dry so no towel is needed

explanation.surface: A whirling holy man who doesn't bother drying himself after bathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating appliance removes water from laundry by centrifugal force, whirling like a dervish.

clue.text: Language group to prohibit familiarity in France

parts.note: to prohibit is to ban
tu is the familiar French word for you

explanation.surface: A language family trying to forbid casual speech in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is a large family of related tongues spoken across central and southern Africa, such as Swahili and Zulu.

clue.text: Witness is a foxy type, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a marten is a small fox-like carnivore of the weasel family

explanation.surface: Someone giving evidence is a sly, cunning character.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, with the final r silent, the animal and the answer sound almost alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek source word meant witness, and early Christian martyrs bore witness to their faith by dying.

clue.text: A lover of Cynara holds against a right of church appointment

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: holds means grips inside, so the poet's name has the next piece put within it

parts.note: Ernest Dowson wrote the poem Cynara, with its refrain about being faithful to her in his fashion
v is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A devoted suitor clinging to his objection to a clerical privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: The lover is the poet speaking in Dowson's Cynara, so the poet's name stands for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Advowson is the legal entitlement in English church law to nominate a priest to a parish living.
